words.definition: a double layer of phospholipids with hydrophilic heads facing water and hydrophobic tails facing inward
words.example: The plasma membrane is based on a phospholipid bilayer.

words.definition: the property of a membrane that allows some substances to cross more easily than others
words.example: Selective permeability helps cells control their internal conditions.

words.definition: passive movement of particles directly through a membrane from higher to lower concentration
words.example: Oxygen can cross many cell membranes by simple diffusion.

words.definition: a difference in the concentration of a substance between two regions
words.example: Particles diffuse down a concentration gradient.

words.definition: a membrane protein embedded in the lipid bilayer, often spanning it
words.example: Channel proteins are integral membrane proteins.

words.definition: a membrane protein attached to the membrane surface rather than embedded deeply in the bilayer
words.example: Peripheral proteins can participate in signalling or cytoskeletal attachment.

words.definition: net movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane from lower solute concentration to higher solute concentration
words.example: Water enters many plant cells by osmosis.

words.definition: a membrane channel protein that allows rapid movement of water molecules
words.example: Aquaporins increase the permeability of membranes to water.

words.definition: a membrane protein that forms a hydrophilic pore allowing specific ions or molecules to cross
words.example: Ion channel proteins allow selected ions to move across membranes.

words.definition: passive movement down a concentration gradient through specific membrane proteins
words.example: Glucose can enter some cells by facilitated diffusion.

words.definition: a membrane transport protein that changes shape to move specific substances across a membrane
words.example: Pump proteins can move ions against their concentration gradients.

words.definition: movement of substances across a membrane against a concentration gradient using energy
words.example: Root cells use active transport to take up some mineral ions.

words.definition: adenosine triphosphate, a nucleotide that transfers usable energy in cells
words.example: ATP provides energy for many active-transport processes.

words.definition: a membrane lipid with a carbohydrate group attached
words.example: Glycolipids contribute to cell recognition at the plasma membrane.

words.definition: the model describing membranes as a fluid phospholipid bilayer containing a mosaic of moving proteins and other components
words.example: The fluid mosaic model explains the dynamic organization of the plasma membrane.

words.definition: a specialized structure within a cell that performs particular functions
words.example: Mitochondria are organelles involved in aerobic respiration.

words.definition: division of a cell into distinct regions where different processes can occur
words.example: Compartmentalization allows incompatible reactions to be separated.

words.definition: a distinct region within a cell, often bounded by a membrane
words.example: The nucleus is an intracellular compartment containing most eukaryotic DNA.

words.definition: a molecule that is produced, used or transformed in metabolism
words.example: Pyruvate is a metabolite produced during breakdown of glucose.

words.definition: a high concentration of particular enzymes within a specific cell compartment
words.example: Keeping enzymes together in an organelle can increase pathway efficiency.

words.definition: cellular reactions that would interfere with each other if they occurred in the same place at the same time
words.example: Compartmentalization separates incompatible reactions inside eukaryotic cells.

words.definition: a membrane-bound compartment formed around material engulfed by phagocytosis
words.example: A phagocytic vacuole can fuse with lysosomes for digestion.

words.definition: a technique used to separate cell components for study
words.example: Cell fractionation can isolate organelles according to size and density.

words.definition: breaking cells or tissues open to produce a uniform mixture called a homogenate
words.japanese: ホモジナイゼーション・均質化
words.example: Homogenization is usually the first step in cell fractionation.

words.definition: separation of particles from a mixture by rapid spinning
words.example: Centrifugation separates cell components according to sedimentation properties.

words.definition: centrifugation at very high speeds to separate very small cellular components
words.example: Ultracentrifugation can separate smaller organelles and macromolecular complexes.

words.definition: the material that collects at the bottom of a centrifuge tube after spinning
words.example: Large cell components form a pellet at lower centrifugation speeds.

words.definition: the liquid remaining above a pellet after centrifugation
words.example: The supernatant can be centrifuged again at a higher speed to isolate smaller components.

words.definition: the process by which an unspecialized cell develops a specialized structure and function
words.example: Cell differentiation produces different cell types from genetically similar cells.

words.definition: a cell with structures and gene activity adapted for a particular function
words.japanese: 特殊化した細胞・分化細胞
words.example: A red blood cell is specialized for oxygen transport.

words.definition: a cell that has not yet developed the structures and functions of a specific mature cell type
words.example: Some stem cells remain unspecialized until they receive signals to differentiate.

words.definition: the use of different sets of genes in different cells or conditions
words.example: Differential gene expression allows cells with the same genome to develop different functions.

words.definition: a spatial difference in the concentration of a chemical signal
words.example: A chemical gradient can influence cell differentiation during development.

words.definition: an unspecialized cell capable of self-renewal and differentiation into one or more cell types
words.example: Stem cells can replace some damaged or lost cells.

words.definition: the local cellular and chemical environment that maintains and regulates stem cells
words.example: Signals from a stem cell niche can control whether a stem cell divides or differentiates.

words.definition: able to produce all cell types of an organism, including extraembryonic tissues
words.example: The earliest embryonic cells are totipotent.

words.definition: able to differentiate into almost any body cell type but not all extraembryonic tissues
words.example: Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent.

words.definition: able to differentiate into a limited range of related cell types
words.example: Blood stem cells are multipotent and can form several types of blood cell.

words.definition: the physical dimensions or volume of a cell
words.example: Cell size is constrained partly by exchange requirements.

words.definition: the amount of surface area available relative to the volume of an object or cell
words.example: Small cells generally have a higher surface area-to-volume ratio than large cells.

words.definition: a surface specialized for movement of substances between an organism and its environment or between compartments
words.example: Alveoli provide a large exchange surface for oxygen and carbon dioxide.

words.definition: the distance particles must travel by diffusion between two regions
words.example: Thin exchange surfaces reduce diffusion distance and increase exchange rate.
